themes.label: Gatekeeper blocks the SDR account-health call
themes.desc: Front desks route the SDR to voicemail, email or a call center, or the office manager is simply never reachable — and a handful of gatekeepers now challenge the account-update pretext as a disguised sales call.
q: typically email is best
I'm going to be very truthful. It's very hard to get in contact with her.

themes.label: Area manager meet-and-greet booked off the SDR check-in motion
themes.desc: The check-in dial continues to convert into booked or agreed virtual area-manager introductions, including one request for an in-person visit; this is the SDR motion's only reliable output.
q: It'd be great if you can come by
Yes, please, yes please. Check the 15, please.

themes.label: Incumbents deny or partially approve; practices stack lenders
themes.desc: The dominant demo driver all month: practices run three to five lenders simultaneously and still see declines or token partial approvals of $250-$1,000 against real treatment plans.
q: They get approved for like a few hundred dollars, which isn't much to cover anything but a cleaning.
I'm familiar. HFD, Cherry, CareCredit, Proceed, Lending Club. All the above.

themes.label: Area manager relationship does not exist
themes.desc: Live providers repeatedly report never having met their assigned area manager, or having lost the only rep they knew to turnover with no handoff; mentions are down sharply this week but so is dial volume into that question.
q: I've never met him.
She told me she's not going to be our rep any more, she'll call us with the new information.

themes.label: Demo and dialer technology failures burn booked time
themes.desc: Booked demos and dials are being lost to Teams/Zoom failures, muted prospects, broken demo portals, dialer audio dropouts, rep swaps, no-shows and forgotten meetings — plus two recordings that ran on past the call and captured private in-office conversation.
q: I totally forgot.
The demo portal for whatever reason isn't wanting to work for me

themes.label: Multi-location, DSO and channel-partner structure
themes.desc: Group practices, DSOs and consultancies split ownership of the HFD relationship across corporate, directors and coordinators, producing duplicate outreach, wasted dials and enrollment tangles.
q: the office managers won't be able to answer that but I can forward your call to the person that's responsible
When I try and onboard two offices, because they're both so similarly named, everything gets all screwed up.

themes.label: Provider does not recognise HFD, including on enrolled accounts
themes.desc: Front desks and office managers at accounts with live HFD records ask who is calling, mistake HFD for an insurance company, or suspect a scam; several inbound leads did not recognise the company they inquired with.
q: What's your company? What type of service do you guys provide
I don't believe we use your services honestly. I've never heard of our office being part of this.

themes.label: Competitor practice fee is the benchmark HFD is measured against
themes.desc: Practices quote incumbent merchant fees of 1.9-5% flat (and 2.3-3.5% on renegotiated plans) as the bar; the one demo this week was the rare case where HFD came out cheaper on the prime tier.
q: I want to say it's about 9%
I think the price of fees are lower. So that's a good thing

themes.label: Financing is a small share of production; patients pay cash
themes.desc: A persistent share of accounts sit in cash-pay, insurance-heavy or Medicaid catchments where patient financing carries well under half — sometimes under 10% — of production, so the approval-breadth pitch has no pull.
q: So most of your demographic, they pay out of pocket. Yeah.
In this area we do less financing than other areas. Patients are more open to paying up front.

themes.label: Explicit enrollment intent on the demo
themes.desc: Prospects asked for the enrollment link or committed to sign on roughly a third of demos in the window; only one such signal landed in the last seven days because almost no demos ran.
q: Beautiful. Where do I sign?
if you can send me the information, that will be great

themes.label: Post-enrollment handoff is failing (dormant, blocked, or unsupported)
themes.desc: Enrollments go missing, portals are never issued, bank connections block transacting, live accounts sit untrained, and reps have no visibility to tell a provider where they stand — reps now ask prospects to email them personally as a manual safety net.
q: I don't have a way to see where you're at.
I literally don't even know how to log in. If you want me to utilize the platform, I would love someone to call me.

themes.label: Referral channels drive the pipeline
themes.desc: Nearly every warm demo traces to an Invisalign rep, a peer doctor, a staff member who used HFD at a DSO, a consultant, or a patient asking the practice to enroll — not to outbound.
q: All of my Invisalign acceptance cases came because of HFD.
she went to a different provider because she was approved for this financing, but we are not participating

themes.label: Volume tier match off a competitor screenshot
themes.desc: The reps' primary pricing lever: start the practice at a tier matching its Cherry or Sunbit standing on proof of volume, in exchange for first look — used on roughly twenty demos this window.
q: It'll prompt you for a screenshot of your Cherry tier. We'll start you at the top tier with us too.
we will start you wherever you are, just as that first look, with that proper documentation

themes.label: In-house financing is the real incumbent
themes.desc: Interest-free in-house plans, not Cherry or CareCredit, are what HFD has to beat at the front desk — staff default to them and several practices route every patient internally.
q: It's in-house. We do very few third-party.
if my staff is quickly defaulting to 0% interest in house then it's kind of hard to compete

themes.label: Live accounts churning or deprioritising HFD
themes.desc: Distinct from prospect objections: several enrolled providers have stopped using HFD, asked for the account to be closed, or been instructed by the owner to use it only after competitor declines — which then inflates their blended fee and reinforces the decision.
q: The doctor has instructed me to not use your financing if I can help it. The fees are just way too much.
Yes, we would like the account to be closed.

themes.label: Inbound leads worked months late
themes.desc: June inbound inquiries were first dialled on 1-3 September; one had already researched HFD and self-disqualified, another asked whether HFD was still in business. Under 5 mentions, so statistically noisy.
q: I believe I did some research and I decided not to go with you guys.
you still a company?

themes.label: Incumbent service and product failures create switching triggers
themes.desc: Cherry chat-only support, a broken 18-month estimator option, failed identity verification, pay-to-approve upsells, unpullable fee reports and CareCredit retroactive interest are the concrete openings reps are winning on.
q: Everything is through chat with them. Some patients don't like that.
the 18-month option just stopped working. It's not on the estimator. And their support is very slow at helping

themes.label: Sales collateral is wrong, missing, or inconsistent
themes.desc: The deep-subprime slide was corrected live on at least five demos, credit bands are absent from the pricing pages, practice fee reads as patient APR, and the one-pagers, APR-by-tier sheet, payment calculator and sandbox that partners keep asking for do not exist or are inconsistently claimed to exist.
q: this slide needs to be corrected, I apologize
is that the only way that you can send information over is through a demo or do you have something generic

themes.label: Approval breadth is the message that closes
themes.desc: The 99% approval rate, the guaranteed minimum instead of a token counter-offer, the 300 FICO floor, ITIN acceptance and HSA/FSA plus patient-chosen payment dates are the specific points that produce enthusiasm.
q: Wow. Hey, I'm like, man, I might do my Invisalign now with you guys.
my patients on the other lender have always asked, can I use my HSA as my monthly payment and they cannot

themes.label: Chairside prequal, apps, PMS integration and portal reporting asks
themes.desc: Consolidated product queue from demos: QR/prequal at the chair, a patient and provider app, Dentrix and PMS posting, a cumulative fees-paid report, per-doctor sub-accounts, family single-loan billing and a staff rewards program.
q: Unless you got a QR code that they can scan while I'm in the room with them. That's how the incumbent does it.
Does this integrate with Dentrix or do we have to have our front desk go in there?

themes.label: 10-15 business day portal setup is the go-live bottleneck
themes.desc: Quoted on more than twenty demos and repeatedly against ready buyers, a practice opening in September and a same-day signer wanting to be live by Saturday — and quoted inconsistently as 7-10 days, 10-15 days and two to three weeks depending on the rep.
q: we have a lot of accounts that are signing up. So the queue is kind of backed up right now
My only concern is just the start time, the wait time. I was hoping to get one office up and going next week

themes.label: Is the practice liable if the patient stops paying?
themes.desc: The single most common demo question, usually driven by a prior lender that clawed back or paid in instalments; the proof-of-treatment condition then raises a secondary HIPAA worry.
q: I want to see if the practice has any financial responsibility to you
we have HIPAA laws and stuff on what we can share

themes.label: Decision gated on the owner or doctor after the demo
themes.desc: The attendee is very often a coordinator, receptionist or office manager who must take the deck to the owner-doctor, so close timing depends entirely on the follow-up email landing complete.
q: I'll let you talk to the powers that may be
I don't want to tell you that we'll start now. I want to review this with the doctor.

themes.label: Practice cannot see or pass on the fee it will be charged
themes.desc: The credit tier and therefore the fee are invisible until the loan activates, so practices must quote treatment blind — and reps are giving flatly contradictory answers on whether the fee can be passed to the patient or only recovered by raising list prices.
q: You won't be able to see what your practice fee is going to be until the application's complete.
I would like to know if there is a way to pass over that 22% merchant fee

themes.label: Reps cannot answer product, pricing or underwriting questions
themes.desc: Deferred-to-email answers on underwriting criteria, refunds, term gating, loan increases, PMS integrations, data retention and practice-type eligibility repeatedly became the thing the deal was waiting on.
q: I know for sure it's FICO and DTI. I'm assuming homeowner. I honestly I don't have the exact answer for you
once I hear back from you, I'll let you know if I'm ready to forward or not

themes.label: Loan lifecycle gaps: refinancing balances, mid-treatment changes, refunds and clawbacks
themes.desc: Practices repeatedly ask to finance an existing or insurance-denied balance, add to a loan mid-treatment, reuse unused approval, or understand refund and cancellation mechanics — all either unsupported or unanswered.
q: the patient has a balance with us and they're willing to pay but they need financing
what documentation do you guys need if someone were to ask for like a refund

themes.label: Smile Advance cohort model is not explainable
themes.desc: Across seven demos neither reps nor prospects could follow the cohort recoupment mechanic; two reps apologised for their own explanation, and every practice that did understand it rejected it because payout depends on continuous new volume and other patients paying.
q: It's confusing, I know. And I'm not the best at explaining it.
you have to have constant new ones rolling in to cover that difference, right?

themes.label: Subprime practice fee (19-22%) is too high
themes.desc: The month's biggest pricing objection — practices do the arithmetic live on a $5,000 subprime case and refuse the ~$1,000 fee — but zero mentions in the last seven days because only one demo ran, not because it resolved.
q: how do you charge someone 22% almost per patient? That's crazy.
if I present a $6500 case, they only get approved for five, we eat 19%

themes.label: Aligner-brand and vertical eligibility gaps
themes.desc: ClearCorrect, Angel and B Smile cases, dental sleep entities, mental health, non-dental specialties and Canada all fall outside the Invisalign flat fee or outside HFD entirely, and the enrollment form's practice-type list blocks some of them.
q: we are mainly doing angel liners, is it possible that for angel we can get similar fees
a lot of them told us that they were denied because it was not available for a dental sleep practice

themes.label: Down payment requirement blocks the patients who need it
themes.desc: The 15% and 30% subprime and deep-subprime down payments (and the $500 tier) are repeatedly named as unworkable for exactly the low-credit patients HFD is meant to serve; one practice dropped a competitor for the same reason.
q: I feel like for subprime that might be a little bit like aggressive.
they don't have money, really low score, and I come up with 30% it would be kind of a little bit difficult

themes.label: Practice declines or defers the area manager introduction
themes.desc: Short staffing, busy seasons, Labor Day, vendor-meeting bans and simple lack of perceived value pushed a large share of the SDR asks out weeks or refused them outright; none recurred in the last seven days.
q: We don't usually meet with anyone. We work straight through lunch. We don't take any meetings
No, no. Like I don't see a need to do that.

themes.label: Funding caps too low for large cases
themes.desc: Full-arch, implant and full-mouth practices with $25K-$140K cases dismiss the $35,000 prime ceiling and the $5,000-$10,000 risk-tier caps outright; one rep volunteered HFD may not be a fit.
q: $10,000 is really nothing for some of these cases that we do
our cases are average like 38 to 42,000

themes.label: Let the practice control which 0% promo terms and offers patients see
themes.desc: Six independent practices asked to expose only the terms whose fee they will absorb, because patients always pick the longest 0% term, which carries the highest practice fee; the toggle is all-or-nothing.
q: on the other lender you can make them only pick like six months or 12 months
I want the offers to come in front of us and not the patient. It's too overwhelming.

themes.label: Let providers opt out of / auto-decline the subprime tier
themes.desc: Practices asked to block approvals below a credit threshold rather than pay the ~21% fee; reps promised a back-end decline switch is in the pipeline, and both sides queried whether it is even legal. Low count but every instance is a HIGH-severity gating ask.
q: can you just have them not approved if it's under a certain credit score?
can we refuse to do the subprime or decline to do the subprime?

themes.label: Channel partners are setting the wrong expectations
themes.desc: Align field reps pitched Smile Advance terms that conflicted with the AE's pricing, claimed HFD pays Invisalign lab fees directly, referred practices with no program framing, and an in-portal ad reached a Canadian provider HFD cannot serve. Under 10 mentions, so noisy, but each cost a demo slot.
q: She said that if we finance through you guys with Invisalign, you guys will pay Invisalign directly.
he didn't explain that part

exec: MIX WARNING FIRST: only one true AE demo ran in the last 7 days (116316234520; 116306711143 was a reschedule, 116315610633 a no-show, 116312327520 a self-disqualified June lead). Every demo-driven theme therefore shows FADING — subprime fee, deck errors, reps-cannot-answer, Smile Advance — because demo volume collapsed, not because the problems resolved. Do not read those arrows as progress. The first action this week is finding out why the AE calendar emptied after 9/02.

The last-7 window is almost entirely Brandon's dial motion, and it is producing exactly two outcomes: gatekeeper blocks (16 of 47 last-7 items, e.g. 116268572282, 116273390999, 116367768706, 116382723243) and booked area-manager introductions (4: 116277436987, 116264470444, 116273577656, 116285448513). Fridays are structurally dead — 116363942003 confirms management is not on site Fridays — so move the 9/04-style block to Tue-Thu and script the email-deflection counter, because that single objection now appears verbatim across a dozen dials.

Post-enrollment handoff remains the most expensive failure in the corpus (31 mentions) and it has changed character since the prior run: it is no longer just dormant accounts, it is money. 116206675569 reports a related med spa account blocked with tens of thousands unfunded, roughly ten unanswered chargebacks, and dozens of unreturned support calls — and it cost HFD that prospect on the call. 115604623450 (bank not connected, no login) and 115019765835 (enrollment and tier-match proof invisible to the AE) are the same root cause: AEs have no account visibility. Escalate 116206675569 by name this week.

Churn inside live accounts is now explicit and fee-driven, which is new evidence rather than a prospect objection: 116200411485 has been told by the owner to use HFD only after two competitors decline, is shopping for a replacement, and the resulting adverse selection makes every HFD transaction land in the top fee band. Add 115500800539 (asked for the account to be closed), 115582470726 (stopped after their area manager left) and 114575799839 (rates now higher than everything else they use). This is a save-play list, not a coaching item.

Route the four decisions that are not coachable: (1) PRICING — the 19-22% subprime practice fee, 17 mentions, plus the contradiction where reps tell prospects opposite things about passing the fee to the patient (115641726094 versus 115019765835), which is a compliance exposure as well as a lost-deal cause; (2) PRODUCT — a practice-level subprime opt-out and per-term 0% promo control, asked for independently by nine practices and already half-promised by reps as 'in the pipeline'; (3) PRODUCT — the $35,000 cap and the 15%/30% subprime down payment, which together disqualify the full-arch segment; (4) MARKETING/OPS — the deep-subprime slide, corrected live on five separate demos (115421293391, 115792345394, 115594794074, 115314772143, 115211317396), should be fixed before the next demo runs.
changed: Demo volume in the trailing 7 days fell to roughly one real AE demo, versus a demo-heavy prior window — this is the dominant change and it drives most FADING labels.

Live-account churn moved from anecdote to explicit evidence: an owner-level instruction to stop using HFD, two account-closure requests, and an unfunded/blocked med spa account with unanswered chargebacks.
The pass-the-fee-to-the-patient question hardened into a documented internal contradiction between the field territory managers and the inside team.
The deep-subprime funding maximum ($5,000 to $3,000) is now being corrected verbally on demos against a stale slide by at least four different reps, and the number in market is inconsistent.
Gatekeeper email-deflection is now the modal SDR outcome and the reps' counter ('I don't want to send a long email') is being used verbatim and repeatedly refused.
New this window: a third-party treatment-coordination service, not the practice, controls the lender mix at one inbound account (116312327520) — a buyer type not seen in the prior run.
